children: Producer prices in Sri Lanka rose 5.0% year-on-year in July 2026 from a revised 4.1% in the previous month and reaching the highest level since May 2023.
Prices in agriculture rebounded to 0.1% from a 10.7% fall in June, particularly for growing of non-perennial crops (3.5% vs -8.2%), and animal production (14.8% vs 10.4%).
Prices also increased for manufacturing (5.3% vs 4.2%), driven by coke and refined petroleum products, which surged 51.5% from 3.5% in June, while rubber and plastics products rose 16.6% from 6%.
In contrast, inflation eased for electricity, gas, steam, and air conditioning supply (23% vs 29.4%), and water collection, treatment and supply (5.5% vs 6.1%).
On a monthly basis, producer prices edged up 0.5% in July, rebounding from a 1.2% drop in June.

title: Sri Lanka Producer Inflation Highest Since 2023
